    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "# Customer Churn Prediction\n",
        "\n",
        "## Project Overview\n",
        "\n",
        "This project uses Python and Machine Learning to analyze customer churn and predict whether a customer is likely to leave a telecommunications service.\n",
        "\n",
        "The project covers the complete data science workflow, including data loading, data cleaning, exploratory data analysis (EDA), feature preprocessing, machine learning, model evaluation, and comparison.\n",
        "\n",
        "## Dataset\n",
        "\n",
        "The dataset used in this project is the IBM Telco Customer Churn sample dataset.\n",
        "\n",
        "It contains customer information such as:\n",
        "\n",
        "- Customer demographics\n",
        "- Services\n",
        "- Contract information\n",
        "- Payment methods\n",
        "- Monthly charges\n",
        "- Total charges\n",
        "- Customer churn status\n",
        "\n",
        "## Objective\n",
        "\n",
        "The main objective is to identify patterns related to customer churn and build machine learning models that can classify customers as likely to churn or not churn.\n",
        "\n",
        "## Technologies\n",
        "\n",
        "- Python\n",
        "- Pandas\n",
        "- NumPy\n",
        "- Matplotlib\n",
        "- Seaborn\n",
        "- Scikit-learn\n",
        "- Google Colab"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "RMkDQhGJPJXS"
      }
    },

        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
        "import seaborn as sns\n",
        "\n",
        "from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\n",
        "from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder\n",
        "from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer\n",
        "from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Libraries imported successfully!\")"
      ]
    },

    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "# Remove columns that should not be used for prediction\n",
        "df_model = df.drop(columns=[\"customerID\", \"tenure_group\"])\n",
        "\n",
        "# Separate features and target\n",
        "X = df_model.drop(columns=[\"Churn\"])\n",
        "y = df_model[\"Churn\"]\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Features:\", X.shape)\n",
        "print(\"Target:\", y.shape)"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "ELd4wS5MTdQn",
        "outputId": "485219ce-b248-45cc-8544-cb97b19a1d15"
      },
      "execution_count": 26,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Features: (7043, 19)\n",
            "Target: (7043,)\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "y = y.map({\"No\": 0, \"Yes\": 1})\n",
        "\n",
        "print(y.value_counts())"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "X-v86lnIThht",
        "outputId": "b8b898a0-1f94-4278-9f68-0a0dbb62ef93"

            "Churn\n",
            "0    5174\n",

          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "numeric_features = X.select_dtypes(include=[\"int64\", \"float64\"]).columns.tolist()\n",
        "categorical_features = X.select_dtypes(include=[\"object\"]).columns.tolist()\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Numeric features:\")\n",
        "print(numeric_features)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"\\nCategorical features:\")\n",
        "print(categorical_features)"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "HOePzZFVTkv-",
        "outputId": "fcd0884c-c915-4873-be01-6724fac22510"
      },
      "execution_count": 28,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Numeric features:\n",
            "['SeniorCitizen', 'tenure', 'MonthlyCharges', 'TotalCharges']\n",
            "\n",
            "Categorical features:\n",
            "['gender', 'Partner', 'Dependents', 'PhoneService', 'MultipleLines', 'InternetService', 'OnlineSecurity', 'OnlineBackup', 'DeviceProtection', 'TechSupport', 'StreamingTV', 'StreamingMovies', 'Contract', 'PaperlessBilling', 'PaymentMethod']\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split\n",
        "\n",
        "X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(\n",
        "    X,\n",
        "    y,\n",
        "    test_size=0.20,\n",
        "    random_state=42,\n",
        "    stratify=y\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Training data:\", X_train.shape)\n",
        "print(\"Testing data:\", X_test.shape)"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "Oh_uapghTzwM",
        "outputId": "630c90fb-7bba-4aa8-e2e7-6ddb9f7e0a8c"
      },
      "execution_count": 29,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Training data: (5634, 19)\n",
            "Testing data: (1409, 19)\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer\n",
        "from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder\n",
        "\n",
        "preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(\n",
        "    transformers=[\n",
        "        (\n",
        "            \"num\",\n",
        "            StandardScaler(),\n",
        "            numeric_features\n",
        "        ),\n",
        "        (\n",
        "            \"cat\",\n",
        "            OneHotEncoder(\n",
        "                handle_unknown=\"ignore\",\n",
        "                drop=\"first\"\n",
        "            ),\n",
        "            categorical_features\n",
        "        )\n",
        "    ]\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Preprocessor created successfully!\")"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "nbIWAuRdT4af",
        "outputId": "e6485cce-c3a9-4861-eab7-ec6ab214c12d"
      },
      "execution_count": 30,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Preprocessor created successfully!\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "X_train_processed = preprocessor.fit_transform(X_train)\n",
        "X_test_processed = preprocessor.transform(X_test)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Processed training shape:\", X_train_processed.shape)\n",
        "print(\"Processed testing shape:\", X_test_processed.shape)"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "tVkzs_jLT8yU",
        "outputId": "5484c888-d48b-4747-d331-48758dceafdb"
      },
      "execution_count": 31,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Processed training shape: (5634, 30)\n",
            "Processed testing shape: (1409, 30)\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression\n",
        "\n",
        "logistic_model = LogisticRegression(\n",
        "    max_iter=1000,\n",
        "    class_weight=\"balanced\",\n",
        "    random_state=42\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "logistic_model.fit(X_train_processed, y_train)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Logistic Regression model trained successfully!\")"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "xr1hUzYAUJnj",
        "outputId": "29b2d315-c09b-4c1c-e09d-42d7508e4da3"
      },
      "execution_count": 32,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Logistic Regression model trained successfully!\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "y_pred = logistic_model.predict(X_test_processed)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(y_pred[:20])"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"

        "from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, classification_report, confusion_matrix\n",

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## First Machine Learning Model: Logistic Regression\n",
        "\n",
        "After cleaning and preprocessing the dataset, the first machine learning model used in this project is **Logistic Regression**.\n",
        "\n",
        "Logistic Regression is a classification algorithm used to predict a categorical outcome. In this project, it is used to predict whether a customer will **churn (`1`)** or **stay (`0`)**. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}\n",
        "\n",
        "### Why Logistic Regression?\n",
        "\n",
        "Logistic Regression is useful as a first model because it provides a simple baseline for a binary classification problem. It also allows us to compare its performance with other machine learning algorithms later in the project.\n",
        "\n",
        "Because the dataset has more customers who stayed than customers who churned, `class_weight=\"balanced\"` was used to give greater weight to the less frequent churn class. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}\n",
        "\n",
        "### Model Configuration\n",
        "\n",
        "The model was trained with:\n",
        "\n",
        "- `max_iter=1000` to allow enough iterations for convergence\n",
        "- `class_weight=\"balanced\"` to account for the imbalanced target classes\n",
        "- `random_state=42` for reproducible results\n",
        "\n",
        "### First Model Results\n",
        "\n",
        "The Logistic Regression model achieved an accuracy of **73.88%** on the test data.\n",
        "\n",
        "For the **Churn = Yes** class:\n",
        "\n",
        "- **Precision:** 51%\n",
        "- **Recall:** 78%\n",
        "- **F1-score:** 61%\n",
        "\n",
        "The recall of 78% means that the model correctly identified a large proportion of the customers who actually churned.\n",
        "\n",
        "The confusion matrix was:\n",
        "\n",
        "| | Predicted No | Predicted Yes |\n",
        "|---|---:|---:|\n",
        "| **Actual No** | 748 | 287 |\n",
        "| **Actual Yes** | 81 | 293 |\n",
        "\n",
        "This first model provides a baseline that will be compared with other machine learning models later in the project."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "Kv0tbrisU-qd"
      }
    },

      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier\n",

        "    class_weight=\"balanced\",\n",
        "    random_state=42\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "random_forest.fit(X_train_processed, y_train)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Random Forest model trained successfully!\")"
      ],

          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Second Machine Learning Model: Random Forest\n",
        "\n",
        "The second machine learning model used in this project is the **Random Forest Classifier**.\n",
        "\n",
        "Random Forest is an ensemble classification method that combines multiple decision trees to make predictions. In this project, it is used to predict whether a customer will churn or stay.\n",
        "\n",
        "### Why Random Forest?\n",
        "\n",
        "Random Forest was selected to provide a second model for comparison with Logistic Regression. This allows us to evaluate whether a tree-based model can capture patterns in the customer data differently from a linear classification model.\n",
        "\n",
        "The model was configured with:\n",
        "\n",
        "- `n_estimators=200` to create 200 decision trees\n",
        "- `max_depth=10` to limit the depth of each tree\n",
        "- `class_weight=\"balanced\"` to account for the imbalance between churn and non-churn customers\n",
        "- `random_state=42` to make the results reproducible\n",
        "\n",
        "The `balanced` setting automatically adjusts class weights according to the class frequencies. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}\n",
        "\n",
        "### Random Forest Results\n",
        "\n",
        "The Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of **76.15%**.\n",
        "\n",
        "For the `Churn = Yes` class:\n",
        "\n",
        "- **Precision:** 54%\n",
        "- **Recall:** 72%\n",
        "- **F1-score:** 62%\n",
        "\n",
        "### Confusion Matrix\n",
        "\n",
        "| | Predicted No | Predicted Yes |\n",
        "|---|---:|---:|\n",
        "| **Actual No** | 803 | 232 |\n",
        "| **Actual Yes** | 104 | 270 |\n",
        "\n",
        "The Random Forest model provides a second result that can be compared with the Logistic Regression baseline."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "mMRNb1rUVh3M"
      }
    },

        "## Model Comparison\n",
        "\n",
        "Two classification models were trained and evaluated:\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Logistic Regression\n",
        "2. Random Forest\n",
        "\n",
        "The models are compared using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score for the **Churn = Yes** class.\n",
        "\n",
        "For this project, recall and F1-score are important because the goal is to identify customers who may churn. Precision measures how many predicted churners actually churned, while recall measures how many actual churners were identified. The F1-score combines precision and recall into a single measure. ([scikit-learn.org](https://sklearn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.classification_report.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))"

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Model Comparison Findings\n",
        "\n",
        "The Random Forest model achieved higher overall accuracy than Logistic Regression, with an accuracy of 76.15% compared with 73.88%.\n",
        "\n",
        "Random Forest also achieved slightly higher precision and F1-score for the churn class.\n",
        "\n",
        "However, Logistic Regression achieved higher recall for the churn class (78% compared with 72%). This means Logistic Regression identified a larger proportion of the customers who actually churned.\n",
        "\n",
        "The results show that the two models have different strengths. Random Forest performed better on overall accuracy and F1-score, while Logistic Regression detected more of the actual churn cases.\n",
        "\n",
        "Further evaluation will be used before selecting a final model, including ROC-AUC and feature importance analysis."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "FE3wFPwuV6-7"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## ROC-AUC Evaluation\n",
        "\n",
        "ROC-AUC measures how well a classification model can distinguish between the two classes across different classification thresholds.\n",
        "\n",
        "For this project:\n",
        "\n",
        "- Class 0 = Customer stays\n",
        "- Class 1 = Customer churns\n",
        "\n",
        "The ROC-AUC score will be calculated for both Logistic Regression and Random Forest using their predicted probability for the churn class."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "ft_SnZuBWIGu"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score\n",
        "\n",
        "# Probability of Churn = 1\n",
        "y_prob_logistic = logistic_model.predict_proba(X_test_processed)[:, 1]\n",
        "y_prob_rf = random_forest.predict_proba(X_test_processed)[:, 1]\n",
        "\n",
        "# Calculate ROC-AUC\n",
        "roc_auc_logistic = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob_logistic)\n",
        "roc_auc_rf = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob_rf)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(f\"Logistic Regression ROC-AUC: {roc_auc_logistic:.4f}\")\n",
        "print(f\"Random Forest ROC-AUC: {roc_auc_rf:.4f}\")"
      ],
      "metadata": {

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## ROC-AUC Evaluation\n",
        "\n",
        "ROC-AUC was calculated to evaluate how well each model can distinguish between customers who churn and customers who stay across different classification thresholds.\n",
        "\n",
        "### Results\n",
        "\n",
        "| Model | ROC-AUC |\n",
        "|---|---:|\n",
        "| Logistic Regression | 0.8418 |\n",
        "| Random Forest | 0.8410 |\n",
        "\n",
        "Both models achieved very similar ROC-AUC scores of approximately 0.84.\n",
        "\n",
        "Logistic Regression achieved a slightly higher ROC-AUC, while Random Forest achieved higher accuracy and F1-score. Logistic Regression also achieved higher recall for the churn class.\n",
        "\n",
        "Because the models have different strengths across the evaluation metrics, ROC-AUC is considered together with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score rather than being used alone to evaluate the models."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "4rZT8hJCWp6C"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.metrics import roc_curve\n",
        "\n",
        "fpr_logistic, tpr_logistic, _ = roc_curve(\n",
        "    y_test,\n",
        "    y_prob_logistic\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "fpr_rf, tpr_rf, _ = roc_curve(\n",
        "    y_test,\n",
        "    y_prob_rf\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.plot(\n",
        "    fpr_logistic,\n",
        "    tpr_logistic,\n",
        "    label=f\"Logistic Regression (AUC = {roc_auc_logistic:.4f})\"\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.plot(\n",
        "    fpr_rf,\n",
        "    tpr_rf,\n",
        "    label=f\"Random Forest (AUC = {roc_auc_rf:.4f})\"\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.plot(\n",
        "    [0, 1],\n",
        "    [0, 1],\n",
        "    linestyle=\"--\",\n",
        "    label=\"Random Classifier\"\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.title(\"ROC Curve Comparison\")\n",
        "plt.xlabel(\"False Positive Rate\")\n",
        "plt.ylabel(\"True Positive Rate\")\n",
        "plt.legend()\n",
        "plt.show()"
      ],

        "## ROC Curve Interpretation\n",
        "\n",
        "The ROC curves for Logistic Regression and Random Forest are very similar.\n",
        "\n",
        "Logistic Regression achieved a ROC-AUC of **0.8417**, while Random Forest achieved **0.8410**. Both models show a clear ability to distinguish between customers who churn and customers who stay, as their curves remain well above the random-classifier baseline.\n",
        "\n",
        "The small difference between the two AUC values indicates that their overall ranking performance is very similar on the test dataset.\n",
        "\n",
        "ROC-AUC is considered together with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score when evaluating the models."
      ],

        "id": "XNDQYxOsW8Iz"

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Feature Importance Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "Feature importance was analyzed using the Random Forest model to identify which input features contributed most to the model's predictions.\n",
        "\n",
        "The most important features were:\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Tenure — 17.46%\n",
        "2. Total Charges — 14.11%\n",
        "3. Monthly Charges — 10.49%\n",
        "4. Contract (Two year) — 9.84%\n",
        "5. Internet Service (Fiber optic) — 6.77%\n",
        "6. Payment Method (Electronic check) — 5.02%\n",
        "7. Contract (One year) — 4.19%\n",
        "\n",
        "The results indicate that customer tenure and billing-related variables contributed strongly to the Random Forest's predictions.\n",
        "\n",
        "These feature-importance values describe how the model used the variables to make predictions. They should not be interpreted as proof that a feature directly causes customer churn."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "AV5j49OqXbCE"
      }
    },

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Permutation Feature Importance\n",
        "\n",
        "Permutation feature importance was used as an additional feature-analysis method.\n",
        "\n",
        "Unlike the built-in Random Forest feature importance, permutation importance measures how much the model's performance decreases when the values of one feature are randomly shuffled.\n",
        "\n",
        "The analysis is performed on the test dataset to examine which features contribute to the model's predictive performance on unseen data."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "FNo-q1maXtwZ"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance\n",
        "\n",
        "# Calculate permutation importance on the test data\n",
        "perm_result = permutation_importance(\n",
        "    random_forest,\n",
        "    X_test_processed,\n",
        "    y_test,\n",
        "    scoring=\"roc_auc\",\n",
        "    n_repeats=10,\n",
        "    random_state=42,\n",
        "    n_jobs=-1\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "# Create a DataFrame\n",
        "permutation_importance_df = pd.DataFrame({\n",
        "    \"Feature\": feature_names,\n",
        "    \"Importance_Mean\": perm_result.importances_mean,\n",
        "    \"Importance_Std\": perm_result.importances_std\n",
        "})\n",
        "\n",
        "# Sort from highest to lowest\n",
        "permutation_importance_df = permutation_importance_df.sort_values(\n",
        "    by=\"Importance_Mean\",\n",
        "    ascending=False\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "permutation_importance_df.head(15)"
      ],

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Permutation Feature Importance Findings\n",
        "\n",
        "Permutation feature importance was calculated on the test dataset using ROC-AUC as the scoring metric.\n",
        "\n",
        "The most important features were:\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Tenure\n",
        "2. Contract — Two year\n",
        "3. Internet Service — Fiber optic\n",
        "4. Contract — One year\n",
        "5. Total Charges\n",
        "\n",
        "Tenure had the largest mean decrease in ROC-AUC when its values were randomly shuffled, indicating that the Random Forest relied substantially on this feature for its predictions on the test data.\n",
        "\n",
        "Contract type, internet service, and total charges also showed meaningful contributions to the model's predictive performance.\n",
        "\n",
        "Permutation importance measures how much the performance of this particular model depends on each feature. Therefore, these results should not be interpreted as evidence that a feature directly causes customer churn."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "6TEQ8aPsYZic"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Final Model Evaluation\n",
        "\n",
        "Two machine learning models were developed for customer churn prediction:\n",
        "\n",
        "- Logistic Regression\n",
        "- Random Forest\n",
        "\n",
        "The models were evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC.\n",
        "\n",
        "These metrics provide different views of model performance. In particular, recall is important when evaluating the ability to identify customers who actually churn, while F1-score summarizes precision and recall. ROC-AUC evaluates the model's ability to distinguish between the two classes across different thresholds."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "f77BSb5eYrQd"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "from sklearn.metrics import (\n",
        "    accuracy_score,\n",
        "    precision_score,\n",
        "    recall_score,\n",
        "    f1_score,\n",
        "    roc_auc_score\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "# Predictions\n",
        "y_pred_logistic = logistic_model.predict(X_test_processed)\n",
        "y_pred_rf = random_forest.predict(X_test_processed)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Probabilities for ROC-AUC\n",
        "y_prob_logistic = logistic_model.predict_proba(X_test_processed)[:, 1]\n",
        "y_prob_rf = random_forest.predict_proba(X_test_processed)[:, 1]\n",
        "\n",
        "# Create comparison table\n",
        "final_results = pd.DataFrame({\n",
        "    \"Model\": [\n",
        "        \"Logistic Regression\",\n",
        "        \"Random Forest\"\n",
        "    ],\n",
        "    \"Accuracy\": [\n",
        "        accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred_logistic),\n",
        "        accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred_rf)\n",
        "    ],\n",
        "    \"Precision\": [\n",
        "        precision_score(y_test, y_pred_logistic),\n",
        "        precision_score(y_test, y_pred_rf)\n",
        "    ],\n",
        "    \"Recall\": [\n",
        "        recall_score(y_test, y_pred_logistic),\n",
        "        recall_score(y_test, y_pred_rf)\n",
        "    ],\n",
        "    \"F1-Score\": [\n",
        "        f1_score(y_test, y_pred_logistic),\n",
        "        f1_score(y_test, y_pred_rf)\n",
        "    ],\n",
        "    \"ROC-AUC\": [\n",
        "        roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob_logistic),\n",
        "        roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob_rf)\n",
        "    ]\n",
        "})\n",
        "\n",
        "final_results.round(4)"
      ],

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Final Findings\n",
        "\n",
        "The project compared Logistic Regression and Random Forest for customer churn prediction.\n",
        "\n",
        "Random Forest achieved higher overall accuracy and F1-score, while Logistic Regression achieved higher recall and a slightly higher ROC-AUC.\n",
        "\n",
        "The results show that the two models have different strengths:\n",
        "\n",
        "- Random Forest achieved 76.15% accuracy and a 0.62 F1-score.\n",
        "- Logistic Regression achieved 73.88% accuracy and a 0.61 F1-score.\n",
        "- Logistic Regression achieved a recall of 0.78 for customers who churned.\n",
        "- Random Forest achieved a recall of 0.72.\n",
        "- Both models achieved a ROC-AUC of approximately 0.84.\n",
        "\n",
        "The feature analysis showed that tenure, contract type, internet service, total charges, and monthly charges were among the more important variables used by the models.\n",
        "\n",
        "Overall, the project demonstrates an end-to-end machine learning workflow, from data cleaning and exploratory analysis to preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and interpretation."
      ],
